### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s).

**37** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b74434c5816520fddfb531e530df15f281992ba7`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 37 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b74434c5816520fddfb531e530df15f281992ba7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a38fb6779290d02f658a5da2afb02598eb200c2e` — the merge of head `f782520bf2b07070a46eba75a2d7bdd11a952a08` into base `b74434c5816520fddfb531e530df15f281992ba7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a38fb6779290d02f658a5da2afb02598eb200c2e && git checkout a38fb6779290d02f658a5da2afb02598eb200c2e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b74434c5816520fddfb531e530df15f281992ba7 f782520bf2b07070a46eba75a2d7bdd11a952a08 && git checkout -B drift-repro b74434c5816520fddfb531e530df15f281992ba7 && git merge --no-ff f782520bf2b07070a46eba75a2d7bdd11a952a08

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b74434c5816520fddfb531e530df15f281992ba7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b74434c5816520fddfb531e530df15f281992ba7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f782520bf2b07070a46eba75a2d7bdd11a952a08`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/api-key-restore-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/api-key-restore-guard.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/forced-reset-revocation.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/forced-reset-revoke-reason-vocabulary.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/managed-extension-fields.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-user-endpoints.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-api-key.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-api-key-single-declaration.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/en.objects.generated.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/zh-CN.objects.generated.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/ja-JP.objects.generated.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/es-ES.objects.generated.ts, packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts, packages/core/src/security/api-key-lifecycle.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/identity-write-guard.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts (`hasPlatformAdminStanding`, `resolveUserAuthzGrants` 6b / 6b-config), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`registerHook` sort, `triggerHooks`, `buildSession`, the `update()` by-id branch: pre-hook readonly hide, the #14088 recorder, the unconditional `readUpdatePriorRow`, the post-hook hand-back; `dispatchPerRowBeforeHooks`), packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts (`stripReadonlyFields`, `isPreservableUnderAudit`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/keys.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-user-endpoints.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/platform-admin-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (PATCH data route), packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts (import routes), packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts (`mapDataError`), docs/adr/0068-unified-user-context-and-built-in-identity-roles.md (D2 and its 2026-10-06 note), docs/adr/0092-sys-user-profile-field-delegation.md (D2, D4), .changeset/pre/23287-api-key-account-posture.md, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs; the diff's three prose paths (.changeset/23993-reset-revoked-key-restore.md, content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx, content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx row 26b) were read too

### ① Derived judgments

**Inputs read.** Card #23993 (body; triage grade 6221482817; claim 6222506660; `blocked` report 6222928785; amendment 6222961246, route A; the dev's `done` report 6224544673; amendment 2 6224565245), #23287 ruling C′ (comment 6159450584) and its pre-changeset line "an administrator can restore a key a routine reset revoked …, or the owner mints a replacement", PR #24044's body and 18-file list, the net diff `origin/main...f782520bf` (merge base `2b274600b`; 654+/16−), and the head's check-runs. The `--paths` recogniser decides no face from the paths alone and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` line, so this is the narrowing face at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.

**Accept-set and public-surface changes, each judged:**

1. **`sys_api_key.revoked_reason` — a widening of the published object (platform-objects).** A `select` with one option (`admin_password_reset`), `required: false`, `readonly: true`, `group: 'Lifecycle'`. RIGHT. `readonly` is the ADR-0092 D4 form-rendering rule for a column outside the D2 whitelist, and the object already declares `managedBy: 'better-auth'` with `apiMethods: ['get', 'list', 'update']` (no `bulk`). Declared in `MANAGED_EXTENSION_FIELDS.sys_api_key` (the D7 collision declaration, where every column of this hand-rolled table belongs) and NOT in `MANAGED_EXTENSION_EDITABLE_FIELDS`, which stays `{revoked}`; the vocabulary test pins both halves and the single-declaration pin gains the column. Four bundles carry label, help and the option label (`en` regenerated, three hand-written; `check:i18n` and `check:i18n-stale-fill` green in Lint & Repo Gates).

2. **The stamp (plugin-auth `forced-reset-revocation.ts`) — a system-context write that now carries the reason.** RIGHT and the only producer: the field is new in this diff, so its writers are exactly the stamp and the guard's clear. `SYSTEM_CTX = { isSystem: true, positions: [], permissions: [] }`; the scan is `where: { user_id, revoked: false }`, so a key already revoked is not written and keeps no reason, which is the truthful reading (see ③-1). `admin-user-endpoints.ts` is untouched; its unit test's DEFAULT ON expectation gains the reason on both rows, as the amendment foresaw.

3. **The restore guard (plugin-auth `api-key-restore-guard.ts`) — the narrowing.** One `beforeUpdate` hook, `object: sys_api_key`, priority 15. Read against the amendment's five rules:
   - *Rule 1, refuse.* A user-context write whose payload owns a `revoked` key with any value that is not `true`/`1`/`'true'`/`'1'` is an un-revoke; if `ctx.previous` is absent or `previous.revoked_reason === 'admin_password_reset'` and `hasPlatformAdminStanding(engine, session.userId)` is false, it throws `{ code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED', status: 403, object: sys_api_key }` naming both roads. RIGHT. Absent-pre-image fails closed, and on the by-id branch `readUpdatePriorRow` is unconditional (engine.ts: "the read is now UNCONDITIONAL", not-found gate throws 404 before `triggerHooks('beforeUpdate')`), so a legitimate owner's plain restore is never refused on a missing `previous`; on the predicate branch `dispatchPerRowBeforeHooks` binds each row's own `previous`.
   - *Rule 2, stamp only on the reset.* Holds (item 2).
   - *Rule 3, clear on every admitted un-revoke.* `data.revoked_reason = null` is written after the refusal check for every context. RIGHT, and it persists: the clear lands inside the #14088 recording window as a hook write, and the post-hook hand-back of a hidden caller value (engine.ts 16740–16760) re-applies only when the key is absent from the payload or holds `undefined`; a hook-written `null` is neither, so a caller-forged `revoked_reason` is never handed back and `hookWrittenKeys` carries the key past the static readonly strip. Measured by the dev (m1) and pinned on the real chain (pin 2, the admin batch, the system un-revoke).
   - *Rule 4, never clear on a re-revoke.* `isUnrevoke` is false, the handler returns before any write, and the caller's `revoked_reason` never reaches the row: D2 at priority 10 deletes every non-whitelisted key from `input.data` on every user-context face, and on ordinary faces the engine's pre-hook hide withholds it even earlier. Pin 4 drives revoke, a forged `revoked_reason: null` beside revoke, then restore. RIGHT.
   - *Rule 5, system never refused.* `isUserContextWrite` is the D2 predicate verbatim (`Boolean(session?.userId) && session?.isSystem !== true`; `buildSession` propagates `isSystem`), so an `isSystem` write skips the refusal; a write that leaves `revoked` alone returns before anything. RIGHT. The `skipAutomations` flag an import sets skips only metadata-bound hooks (`entry.meta`), never this code-registered one.

4. **The registration (`auth-plugin.ts`).** In the same `kernel:ready` block, after `registerIdentityWriteGuard`, with a distinct `packageId`. RIGHT: the engine sorts hook entries ascending by priority ("lower runs first"), so D2 (10) always precedes the guard (15) regardless of registration order; the pin boots `start()` and asserts one `beforeUpdate` on `sys_api_key` at a priority greater than D2's 10. No other code-registered `beforeUpdate` hook targets `sys_api_key`; the two global ones (approvals lifecycle at default 100, member-role canonicalization at 5 scoped to `sys_member`) write neither `revoked` nor `revoked_reason`.

5. **`API_KEY_REVOKED` message (core `api-key.ts`).** Branches on `row.revoked_reason`; `row` is `any` from an unprojected system `ql.find('sys_api_key', { where: { key }, limit: 1 })`, so the column arrives. Code, status, `keyId`/`userId` and ordering unchanged; the reason-row text names only a platform administrator and `POST /api/v1/keys`. RIGHT; pinned in core (pin 6) and end to end through `resolveApiKeyAdmission` in the guard test. The error catalog's `API_KEY_REVOKED` entry moves with it.

6. **Public surface.** `registerApiKeyRestoreGuard` and `API_KEY_RESTORE_GUARD_PRIORITY` are not re-exported from plugin-auth's `index.ts`; `FORCED_RESET_REVOKE_REASON` keeps its value; no `packages/spec` change, no new route, permission set, role or error code. The new census row 26b anchors the guard's one `isSystem` read site (`check:system-context-census` green).

**Security — can a non-platform-admin user-context write clear `revoked` on a reset-revoked key, or clear or forge `revoked_reason`?** No, on every face I could reach:
- *Direct PATCH.* `PATCH /api/v1/data/sys_api_key/{id}` resolves the caller's context (`resolveExecCtx`, never `isSystem`), calls `p.updateData` by id, the engine binds `previous`, D2 runs, the guard throws; `mapDataError`'s declared-status passthrough answers 403 as it does for D2's own refusals. Pin 1.
- *`multi: true`.* No caller face carries it: the PATCH handler passes no `multi`/`where`; `/data/:object/batch` and `/updateMany` are gated on `'bulk'`, absent from `apiMethods`. At the engine, each matched row is judged on its own `previous`, a throw refuses the whole batch before any write, and the clear is keyed on the payload and assigned in place, so the #14099 key-set divergence cannot fire. Three pins.
- *Import update.* `POST /data/sys_api_key/import` with `writeMode: update` passes the method gate (`update` is open), but `runImport`'s `writeCtx` spreads the CALLER's context plus `skipAutomations` (and `preserveAudit`/`skipStateMachine` under `treatAsHistorical`) and writes through `p.updateData({ id: target.id, … })`, the same by-id path with D2 and the guard. One nuance the PR body overstates: under `preserveAudit`, `stripReadonlyFields` keeps any non-`system` readonly field the caller supplies (`isPreservableUnderAudit`: `def.system !== true`), so the engine's pre-hook hide does NOT withhold a caller-sent `revoked_reason` on a historical import; D2 removes it, and the guard reads the reason from `previous`, never from the payload. Two layers on ordinary faces, one (D2) on that face; no face clears or forges it.
- *`revoked_reason` sent alone.* Hidden by the pre-hook strip, or deleted by D2, whose `editableRemaining === 0` branch answers 403 "None of the submitted fields (revoked_reason) are editable"; the guard returns early (no `revoked` key).
- *Owner re-revoke then restore.* Rule 4; pin 4.
- *Other faces.* MCP's data tools call `bridge.update(object, id, data)` as the authenticated principal (no `isSystem` anywhere in `packages/mcp`); the `revoke_api_key`/`restore_api_key` actions are `type: 'api'` client-issued PATCHes with no server-side runner (grep for `type === 'api'`/`bodyExtra` in rest, runtime and core: none); there is no `skipHooks`/`bypassHooks` option anywhere in packages. An `organization_admin` (wildcard `modifyAllRecords`) is a user-context non-platform-admin and is refused like the owner, which is the ruled narrowing, not a hole.
- *Hook ordering.* Refusal and clear live in one handler, refusal first; D2 precedes it; nothing after priority 15 writes the reason on this object.

**Lockout — can a platform administrator be locked out of restoring?** Not a platform administrator by ADR-0068 D2 as amended on 2026-10-06: `hasPlatformAdminStanding` is a fail-closed projection of `resolveUserAuthzGrants`, answering the `PLATFORM_ADMIN` rung (an active unscoped `admin_full_access` grant under the `single` posture, or the verified `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` anchor under every posture), awaited with the registered engine and the session's user id; pin 2 and the admin batch drive the grant route on the real `SecurityPlugin` with `bootstrapPlatformAdmin`'s grant. One asymmetry is real and is flagged in ③-3: the reset endpoint's gate (`judgePlatformAdmin` → `isPlatformAdminUser`) admits the rung OR the legacy `user.role === 'admin'` scalar, while the guard admits the rung only.

**System context — can the mint, the `last_used_at` stamp or the reset be refused?** No. The mint is a single `ql.insert` with `isSystem: true` (`keys.ts:297`), which `beforeUpdate` never sees; `stampAdmittedKey` writes `last_used_at`/`expires_at` only under `isSystem: true`, so the guard returns before the context test; the reset writes `revoked: true`, not an un-revoke. The only non-test writer of `revoked: false` in packages is the mint's insert, so row 26b's "no system writer restores a key" is measured, not assumed. Pinned by the system-context case.

**Non-blocking observations (no action owed on this PR):** (i) on a multi-row admin un-revoke, D2 at priority 10 sees the previous row's hook-written `revoked_reason: null` in the shared payload on rows 2..N, deletes it and logs a "stripped non-whitelisted field(s) … revoked_reason" warning before the guard re-adds it; behaviour is correct (pinned: every row clears) and the face is engine-only, so the diagnostic is noise, not a defect. (ii) ADR-0092 D2's prose says "import's engine calls … bypass the guard unchanged"; the import runner as it stands carries the caller's context, so the guard applies. That is a docs/ADR drift observation on a Tier H surface, not this PR's, named for the seat.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23993-reset-revoked-key-restore.md`: `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/core` at `minor`, a `!` title with a **BREAKING** banner, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, and one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`; the PR body carries the same `Clause-②` line. By `clause2-line.mjs`'s arm grammar `yes (narrowing)` is "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another"; by AGENTS.md `yes` takes at least `minor` and `(narrowing)` is BREAKING, shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention (`check:changeset-no-major`, `check:adr-0087-registration`, `check:empty-changeset` green under Check Changeset / Lint & Repo Gates). The grades match what the diff publishes: platform-objects widens (one field, four bundles), plugin-auth narrows (the write door) and gains no public export, core changes one message's text with no signature change. No other released package publishes anything from this diff; `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/spec` are untouched. The #23287 pre-changeset is not edited; its sentence stands and this changeset narrows "an administrator" to a platform administrator, consistent with triage's reading. The ADR-0087 disposition is right: nothing authorable is removed or renamed, and the refused call's remedy is a person or a new key, not a rewrite. The migration prose the convention asks of a breaking changeset is present ("Refused now / Unchanged / Keys revoked by a forced reset before this release"). Level and arm: RIGHT.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **A key the owner revoked BEFORE the forced reset is not stamped** (dev's acceptance note). Answer: correct as built and truthful by the stamp's own semantics (the reset did not revoke that key), and inside the ruled text, which speaks of keys "a routine reset revoked". The residual (an attacker holding the owner's later session could restore a key the owner had parked) is bounded exactly as triage bounded P1: the reset also ends every session, so only the legitimate owner's later sign-in reaches the door. Whether the reset should also stamp already-revoked keys is a product decision this card does not carry. ESCALATED to the `domain:engine` seat as a follow-up card candidate (`security`, not blocking), not to the maintainer: no ruling text is contradicted.

2. **The Restore API Key action still renders for the owner on a reset-revoked key** (dev's acceptance note). Answer: accepted; the server refuses with the road, and the action's `type: 'api'` PATCH has no server-side runner, so nothing beyond courtesy is missing. A `visible` predicate would need the row's `revoked_reason` beside the caller's standing and is UI work. ESCALATED to the seat as a low-priority follow-up (platform-objects action predicate, with objectui if the console needs it).

3. **Reset gate vs restore gate.** `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/set-user-password` is gated by `judgePlatformAdmin`, which admits `isPlatformAdmin === true` (the rung) OR the legacy `role === 'admin'` scalar; the restore guard admits the rung only. A legacy-scalar-only administrator can therefore stamp keys they cannot restore; such a user is not a platform administrator under ADR-0068 D2 (2026-10-06 note: gates judge by the rung), the restore side is the narrower of the two, and the owner's replacement road stays open, so this is not a hole and not a lockout of a platform administrator. It does make the #23287 sentence "an administrator can restore" false for that one back-compat population. ESCALATED to the seat: either accept (the legacy fallback is documented back-compat and the claim named `hasPlatformAdminStanding`) or carry a follow-up to align the reset gate to the rung. Not blocking.

4. **Pre-existing rows** (changeset and PR body): keys a forced reset revoked on `@objectstack/plugin-auth@18.0.0-next.2` or a `main` build since 2026-10-14 carry no reason and stay owner-restorable; no backfill because the reset's audit row records counts, not ids. Answer: accepted; the population is prerelease-only and the changeset says so to consumers. No decision owed.

5. **The duplicated `isUserContextWrite` predicate** (dev's note; D2's copy is module-private). Answer: accepted; the census row 26b anchors the new read site, and the two bodies are byte-equivalent. Exporting D2's copy would widen plugin-auth's surface for one caller; either way is fine.

6. **Deviation: `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 26b outside the claimed surface.** Answer: declared by amendment 2 to `domain:devx`; the row names the one elevation read and what is gained and lost, and `check:system-context-census` is green. Accepted.

7. **ADR-0092 D2 prose vs the import runner** (①, observation ii). ESCALATED to the seat for the maintainer's attention at their discretion (Tier H surface); not this PR's.

**CI on the head at read time.** 26 check-runs success, 5 skipped, 8 still `in_progress`: Build Core; Test Core (1/6), (2/6), (3/6), (4/6), (5/6), (6/6); Type Check · workspace. Concluded green among the required contexts: Lint & Repo Gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Type Check · source gates / debt ledger / consumer gates, Build Docs. The eight unconcluded checks are not judged here; their conclusions are the gate verdicts and the queue waits for them. The PR touches no governed surface (file list), so no Tier H word is owed.

Reviewed-by: `session_01TQLy3Yq6vF4SDpTXdr3Uwi`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 · ✅ ACCEPT: PR #24044 at `f782520bf2` · `domain:engine` seat 2 · `session_01TQLy3Yq6vF4SDpTXdr3Uwi` · 2026-10-16T21:27Z

**Basis:**
- the claim 6222506660 on #23993 and its amendments 6222961246 (route A, the surface moved to `plugin-auth`) and 6224565245 (the `system-context.mdx` row 26b);
- triage's first grade 6221482817, and #23287 ruling C′ with its changeset's restorer sentence;
- the declarations to `domain:services` (6222520301, 6222967697 on #21118) and to `domain:devx` (6222531655, 6224571469 on #20163), with no objection on any;
- the dev's `blocked` report 6222928785 and `done` report 6224544673;
- the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record 6224996826 (**PASS**, the narrowing face), adopted after a tool-use audit of its transcript: 84 read-only shell calls and 3 reads, one write (the record file), no MCP call and no git write;
- the seat's own reading of the guard, the stamp and the registration, against `origin/main`.

**Checklist**
- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #23993` on line 1. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is on its own line, once, in the body and in the changeset. No other number carries a closing verb.
- **Why `yes (narrowing)`.** `sys_api_key` gains a published field (`revoked_reason`, readonly `select`, one option), which widens. The update door refuses a non-platform-administrator's un-revoke of a key a forced reset revoked, which narrows. `platform-objects`, `plugin-auth` and `core` go `minor` under a **BREAKING** banner. No `packages/spec` change, no new route, permission set, role or error code. ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: nothing authorable moves, and the refused call's remedy is a person or a new key.
- **Ruling C′ is honoured.** Only a platform administrator (`hasPlatformAdminStanding`, the ADR-0068 D2 rung, fail-closed) restores a key the reset revoked. The owner's road is a new key through `POST /api/v1/keys`. The owner's own revocation stays owner-restorable. The `API_KEY_REVOKED` message names the road for the reason-row, and its code, status and fields are unchanged; the error catalog moves with it.
- **The guard fails safe.** It is one `beforeUpdate` hook at priority 15, after D2 at 10 (the engine sorts by priority, so registration order cannot reorder them). An absent `previous` refuses. A system-context write is never refused (the D2 predicate verbatim; census row 26b anchors the one `isSystem` read). The reason clears on every admitted un-revoke and never on a revoke.
